content.text: Section 6.9's audit right runs in our favour (Sanofi auditing RevMed), so it is not in scope. The operative audit right binding us is Section 9.9, which is reciprocal and contains every material protection the rule seeks.

input.quote: Upon reasonable prior notice of the other Party, but in any event at least [***] prior notice, each Party shall and shall cause its Affiliates and its and their Sublicensees to permit an independent auditor of international prominence, selected by the auditing Party and reasonably acceptable to the audited Party, to audit the books and records maintained pursuant to Section 9.8 for the sole purpose of verifying for the auditing Party the accuracy of the financial reports furnished by the audited Party pursuant to this Agreement or of any payments made, or required to be made, by or to the audited Party pursuant to this Agreement or any Ancillary Agreement.
input.rationale: Section 9.9 (Audit Procedures) is the only audit right binding Sanofi as the audited party, and it is fully reciprocal. It meets the preferred position on each material term: (i) frequency is capped at a stated number of times per Calendar Year (p0416); (ii) advance written notice is required ("at least [***] prior notice"); (iii) the audit must be performed by an "independent auditor of international prominence" that is reasonably acceptable to the audited Party, not by RevMed personnel; (iv) the auditor is expressly barred from disclosing the audited Party's Confidential Information beyond the payment discrepancy and must sign a confidentiality agreement with the audited Party (p0417, p0419); (v) the auditing Party "shall bear the full cost of such audit" unless the audit reveals an underpayment exceeding a stated percentage threshold, in which case the audited Party reimburses (p0418); and (vi) the scope is limited to the books and records maintained under Section 9.8 (p0414) with a defined look-back period plus a waiver of stale claims — there is no right of direct or remote access to Sanofi systems, so the walk-away scenario is not present. Two minor points are noted but not flagged: the frequency, notice, look-back and underpayment percentages are redacted ([***]) so the exact figures cannot be confirmed against the 30-day / 5% preferred parameters, and the frequency cap carries an "unless for cause" exception. These are sub-elements short of the ideal wording rather than failures of the fallback, and the clause's mutuality means any tightening would equally cut back our own audit rights over RevMed's Net Profit/Net Loss and cost reporting. No redline recommended; we should confirm the bracketed figures land at no more than once per Calendar Year, at least 30 days' notice and a 5% underpayment threshold when the schedule is unredacted.
